newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Managers November index falls.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Managers November index falls.

text.p: The National Association of Purchasing Management-Metro Detroit's composite November index fell to 52.3 from 59.7 in October, according to a Comerica Inc survey released Thursday.
An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 suggests expansion, according to the survey of southeastern Michigan's industrial economy.
The prices paid index was 51.3 in November versus 52.9 in October. The employment component of the barometer was 55.3 in November versus 55.5 in October.
The November index is 3.0 points higher than a year ago.

"November's decline represents the third consecutive month of decelerating business conditions reported by local purchasing agents," according to David Littmann, senior economist with Detroit-based Comerica Bank.

"The latest survey is somewhat troubling on two counts," Littmann noted. "November is the bellwether survey month, typically indicating the economic pattern for the coming year, and November softening occurred in both automotive and non- automotive sectors."
